rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.fn` only declares the signature `Sources::search_text(&self, &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError>`, which is async. It states no behavior of its own. The behavior and inputs live in the sibling requirements `search_text.behavior` and `search_text.inputs`, and I did not assess those here.

The marked test `tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` calls `Sources::search_text` directly. It passes `&TextQuery` values and awaits the result on a `Sources` value. It asserts both outcomes of the `Result`:
- **`Ok` outcome:** it unwraps the result and checks `complete`, `matches.len()` and `matches[0].path`. These show the returned `TextMatches` carries `complete`, `matches` and per-match `path` fields.
- **`Err` outcome:** it asserts `.is_err()` for the out-of-root scope `SourceScope::under("..")`.

Because the code compiles against this call shape, the compiler enforces the method receiver, the async return and the `Result` shape.

The second marked test, `src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]`, runs `search_text` through the tool session over a 1500-line file. It also exercises the paging path.

The compiler pins the signature, so I found no further obligation in the subject text that needs a separate test. The one thing the compiler does not pin is the concrete error type `SourceError`, because the tests only check `is_err`. I judged that too minor to count as a gap for a signature-only requirement.

text: pub async fn search_text(&self, query: &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError>;
